name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
left: Blue Ghost lander and ten NASA instruments
fact: Firefly Aerospace's Blue Ghost touched down upright on 2 March 2025, within its 100 m target, after a nine-minute braking burn and a final descent on its small thrusters at about 1 m/s. NASA cameras on the lander filmed its plume hitting the surface. It worked for more than 14 days, watched Earth eclipse the Sun from the Moon on 14 March, and sent its last data after sunset on 16 March.
capability: A commercial lander delivered NASA science to the surface and ran it through a full lunar day, returning more than 119 GB of data.
